candidates.title: Why a 155 km/h fastball followed by a 140 km/h slider changes the at-bat
candidates.score_rationale: Uses an existing fact-backed baseball data capsule and can bridge to ScriptBeatIR, visual scene planning, and YMM4 readiness without live media.
candidates.channel_angle: sports news explainer: one pitch sequence becomes a short tactical story
candidates.attribution_note: Derived from repo-local synthetic baseball fixture, not an official league feed or player media source.
excluded_claims: No claim about a real player, team, game, or broadcast footage.
No scouting conclusion beyond the sample pitch-sequence facts.
No publication readiness or rights clearance.
candidates.hook: 速球のあとに球速を落とすと、打者の見え方はどう変わるのか。
candidates.why_it_matters: A concrete pitch-change example gives viewers a fast, visual explanation without relying on licensed footage.
beat_outline: Establish inning, count, score, and empty bases.
Compare the previous 155 km/h four-seam fastball with the current 140 km/h slider.
Explain the 15 km/h drop as the main tactical contrast.
Show the low-outer strike result as the viewer watch point.
Hand off to CSV/Writer IR only after source and claim review.
candidates.recommended_tone: fast tactical yukkuri explainer with light reaction beats
candidates.likely_audience: baseball viewers who like quick tactical breakdowns
candidates.channel_fit: short sports-news yukkuri explainer, under 3 minutes
candidates.visual_motif: Original scoreboard strip plus two pitch cards connected by a speed-drop arrow.
forbidden_avoid_claims: Do not imply this is real broadcast analysis.
Do not use official logos, player photos, or broadcast stills.
Do not call the pitch sequence a proven strategy outside the sample.
candidates.source_rights_caution: Use only original data-card graphics unless a real-source rights record is added later.
candidates.designer_note: Keep the thumbnail numeric and graphic-first: speed drop, pitch-type change, and low-outer target.
